visual_comparison.title: Gregg's catclaw: hooks, cream spikes, and actual seeds
visual_comparison.subtitle: Study exactly where the curved catclaws protrude and how the twice-compound leaves attach.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: HOOKED PRICKLES + ELONGATED CREAM SPIKES. Small leaflets support Gregg; measure before separating Wright.

items.label: BOTH HOOKED PRICKLES
items.image_role: large woody stem with two strongly recurved lateral prickles and bipinnate leaves
items.caption: The large curved projections belong to the stem itself: prickles, not the same as paired straight stipular spines of Vachellia. Small oval leaflets can be seen on fine pinnae around the twig. Hooked prickles identify the CATCLAW group, not Gregg's species alone.
items.creator: Stan Shebs

items.label: GREGG'S · CREAM FLOWER SPIKE
items.image_role: elongated cream inflorescence plus multiple tiny obovate leaflets
items.caption: A SPIKE is an elongated cluster of many tiny flowers, not a round ball. On this one view, the flower spike sits beside small oval leaflets. Compare Roemer's almost spherical pale heads.
items.creator: Sue in az
items.annotation_status: Visible large structures checked on original 1000 × 750 equivalent reference image; pixel relative, exclude microscopic claims.

items.label: GREGG'S · SEEDS & SCALE
items.image_role: six brown flattened mature seeds and a 1 cm ruler
items.caption: This photo shows individual hard seeds removed from a pod. Seeds are NOT the flat mature pod. The 1 cm scale makes this a good anatomy lesson, but seeds alone aren't enough to separate Gregg's from Wright's.
items.creator: Steve Hurst / USDA-NRCS PLANTS Database
items.annotation_status: Clear large seeds + labeled 1 cm source ruler at native 900 × 600 reference; no unverified micromorphology.
